responses.evidence: Prior d3/error path used denylist+length-cap `sanitizeErrorMessage` and CLI `forceError: err.message` (core/scripts/factory-status.ts; pipeline.ts factory-status catch). Residual free text after partial redaction is not a remote-safe contract: adversarial messages can still carry non-matching secrets or prompt-like text into JSON/human/stderr. Revised d3: public `error` and source `__error` projection emit only a closed allowlisted error-code set (same allowlist discipline as next_action/wait kinds); assembler, source-error, and CLI pre-assembly catch paths all map through that code table; canary matrix must cover every path and canary position. Exception detail stays in logs, not the envelope.

Confirmed gap: `startIndependentHeartbeat` and supervisor cycle write-failure handlers only `setRecord({ heartbeat_write_error })` after the process-identity write throws (factory-status.ts ~1383-1390; supervisor.ts ~2765-2771, ~2822-2827). A separate `pipeline factory status` process re-reads durable supervisor.json, still sees a prior fresh `heartbeat_at` within the 90s bound, and can report healthy/live liveness - so in-memory `heartbeat_write_error` is not a durable failure channel. Revised d4: on heartbeat write failure, write a durable side-channel failure marker (distinct path/seam from the process-identity record); status reads that marker and classifies `write_failed`/non-healthy even when last successful heartbeat_at is still fresh; in-memory-only error is not authority for status.

Independent cadence does not require cooperative yields inside dispatch body. `driveSupervisor` starts `startIndependentHeartbeat` as a concurrent async task before the cycle loop (supervisor.ts ~2696-2708). Long item work is `await deps.dispatchItem(...)` (Promise seam, supervisor.ts ~1879) - production dispatch waits on harness child/I/O and yields the Node event loop, allowing the heartbeat sleep/write loop to run. Recovery backoff explicitly sleeps in chunks on a separate `recoverySleep` channel while the independent heartbeat continues. Unit tests exercise injectable cadence and stop (factory-status.test.ts independent heartbeat cases). Decision does not claim progress under multi-second synchronous CPU monopolization of the event loop (that would stall the whole controller); that is outside the Promise-based dispatch model.

Prior d5/`classifyFactoryHealth` treated same-host + `pidAlive === false` as sufficient for `dead` (factory-status.ts ~647-650, ~697-698) with probes limited to hostname + isPidAlive. That is underspecified for service-managed controllers and PID reuse: a restarted service leaves the old pid absent while a new controller/service remains live; a reused pid that is alive without boot_id binding is not proof of the recorded controller. Revised d5: authoritative binding is (hostname, pid, boot_id) plus optional service_controller; `dead` requires stale heartbeat, same-host, identity-bound process absence, and when service identity is present joint service absence or proof the service is not running the recorded controller identity; running service with replaced process -> `unknown` not `dead`; PID-alive without boot/service binding -> `unknown`; injected classification matrix covers those cases.

Prior d6 only concretely owned whole-item `dispatch` waits (supervisor dispatch start ~1865-1877) and `recovery_backoff` (~2809-2830). Types list ci/provider_cooldown/dependency/capacity/human (loop/types.ts `LoopExpectedWaitKind`) and classification tests inject those kinds, but no process-identity writers existed for capacity_wait, human hold, dependency idle, CI wait, or provider cooldown - so acceptance healthy-waiting paths lacked an owned contract. Revised d6: `markControllerOperation` is the sole writer; each acceptance kind has a named set/hold/clear lifecycle (dispatch, recovery_backoff, capacity, human, dependency, ci, provider_cooldown) without raw reason text; nested waits during dispatch may specialize expected_wait_kind while keeping operation deadline for stuck detection; missing upstream deadlines use bounded documented defaults rather than omitting deadlines.

decisions.title: Pure allowlisted assembler over injected readers
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`assembleFactoryStatus`, `FactoryStatusSources`, `FactoryStatusProbes`, `FactoryStatusClock`); CLI wiring in core/scripts/pipeline.ts; OpenSpec design Decision 1

alternatives.option: Persist a second durable factory-status ledger that status writes and re-reads
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires zero mutation of ledger/events/run artifacts; a write path would make status a control surface and couple observability to a new durable schema.

alternatives.option: Expose the raw loop-store status projection as the remote/CLI contract
alternatives.rejected_because: Loop status and supervisor records include lock tokens and unbounded free text; issue non-goals forbid shipping raw loop status over remote-safe surfaces.

assumptions: Existing controller/process, loop status, pin, provider, write-health, and cost sources can be projected through injected seams without live network/git/subprocess in unit tests.
CLI is responsible only for mapping filesystem/config into seams and printing the envelope.
invariants: `assembleFactoryStatus` is pure: no GitHub, git, service, control, ledger, event, or run-artifact mutation.
Unit tests inject clocks, process probes, and source objects; no real network/git/subprocess.
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts module header and `assembleFactoryStatus` docs: pure function over injected sources/clock/probes.
openspec/changes/factory-aggregate-status-and-controller-health/design.md Decision 1.
core/test/factory-status.test.ts: zero-mutation and injected-seam tests.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not replace scoreboard (#301), per-issue status (#154), audit logs, or run artifacts; does not implement HTTP/MCP exposure of the raw store.
decisions.uncertainty: Low for purity requirement (acceptance-bound). Medium that the narrow #890 macro-controller source shape will remain stable; falsified if #890 records require status-side writes or non-injectable I/O.

decisions.title: Versioned envelope with ok/degraded/error and additive v1 fields

alternatives.option: Throw unstructured stderr-only failures for machine consumers
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires exactly one unfenced versioned JSON object including structured error/degraded states parseable via `JSON.parse(stdout)`.

alternatives.option: Bump schema_version on every additive optional field
alternatives.rejected_because: Design allows optional/unknown-safe additives within schema_version "1" so legacy and partial sources stay readable without forcing consumer version churn.

assumptions: Partial source failure should surface as degraded with per-source attribution rather than look fully healthy.
Total assembly failure still emits a valid error envelope.
invariants: `schema_version` is the string `"1"` for this contract.
Top-level `status` is exactly `ok` | `degraded` | `error`.
Missing optional sources are attributed (`unknown` / `legacy` / `not_applicable` / `error`), not silently invented as healthy presence.
Top-level `error` (when present) is an allowlisted error code only — never residual free text (see d3).
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts: `FACTORY_STATUS_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1"`, `FactoryStatusTopLevel`, forceError error-envelope path.
openspec/changes/factory-aggregate-status-and-controller-health/design.md Decision 2.
core/test/factory-status.test.ts: error/degraded envelope and missing-source attribution tests.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Additive optional fields stay on v1 only while they remain optional/unknown-safe; breaking renames or required new fields need a schema bump.
decisions.uncertainty: Low. Falsified if a consumer needs a hard break (required new field with no unknown default) without a version change.

decisions.title: Allowlist-built public envelope; free text dropped; errors are allowlisted codes only
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`FACTORY_STATUS_PUBLIC_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, `FACTORY_STATUS_SOURCE_KEYS`, `sanitizeNextActionCode`, `sanitizeWaitKind`, `mapFactoryStatusErrorCode` replacing free-text `sanitizeErrorMessage` residual paths, `projectLoopSourcesForFactoryStatus`); canary suite in core/test/factory-status.test.ts; CLI catch path in core/scripts/pipeline.ts factory-status handler

alternatives.option: Regex/denylist redaction alone over the raw loop status JSON
alternatives.rejected_because: Denylist is incomplete against new secret shapes and free-text prompt injection; acceptance requires an explicit allowlist and canary proof that secrets and instruction-like text never appear.

alternatives.option: Pass through issue titles, hold reasons, comments, and next-action prose for operator richness
alternatives.rejected_because: Remote-safe contract forbids unsanitized issue/comment/reason text and instruction-like free text in JSON, prose, and error paths.

alternatives.option: Cap and denylist-redact thrown error messages into the public `error` field (prior d3 wording)
alternatives.rejected_because: Residual free text after partial redaction still can carry canaries, credentials, or prompt-like instructions on assembler, source-__error, and CLI pre-assembly catch paths; remote-safe contract requires fixed allowlisted error codes only.

assumptions: Operators can obtain rich free text from existing audit/logs/status surfaces; factory status is the coarse remote-safe projection.
Registered source keys must each receive canary fixtures so new sources cannot skip the guard silently.
A closed set of factory-status error codes is sufficient for machine consumers; operators use logs for exception detail.
invariants: Only named public fields are assembled; source objects are never dumped wholesale onto the envelope.
Lock/bearer tokens, credentials, secret refs, env maps, prompts, tool dumps, and raw supervisor token fields never copy into the public model.
Next-action free text maps to an allowlisted coarse code (or `unknown`); wait kinds map to ALLOWED_WAIT_KINDS only.

Public error surfaces (`envelope.error`, human error line, and any status stderr that echoes the envelope) emit only allowlisted error codes (e.g. `status_assembly_failed`, `primary_source_unavailable`, `loop_status_unavailable`, `pin_unavailable`, `heartbeat_write_failed`, `probe_unavailable`, `unknown_error`) — never source exception messages, never redacted residual free text.
Source `{ __error }` inputs are mapped through the same code allowlist before attribution/detail use; raw `__error` strings never appear in JSON/human/stderr.
Canary matrix covers: every source key, forceError paths, CLI catch-before-assembly path, and canaries at start/middle/end of adversarial exception strings.
evidence: Prior implementation used `sanitizeErrorMessage` denylist+cap (factory-status.ts) and pipeline.ts `forceError: err.message` — insufficient per challenge cf944659; revised contract replaces residual free-text errors with allowlisted codes.
Allowlist pattern already proven for next_action (`ALLOWED_NEXT_ACTION_CODES`) and wait kinds (`ALLOWED_WAIT_KINDS`).
openspec/.../design.md Decision 3 intent (allowlist over denylist); this revision tightens the error sub-contract.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not sanitize or redefine non-factory-status surfaces (audit, logs, evidence bundles, scoreboard). Coarse keyword mapping in `sanitizeNextActionCode` remains intentionally lossy. Exception detail stays in process logs, not the remote envelope.
decisions.uncertainty: Low on the remote-safety requirement. Medium that the closed error-code set will need a few additive codes as real CLI failure modes appear; additive codes stay within schema_version "1" when optional consumers treat unknown codes as `unknown_error`.

decisions.title: Independent controller heartbeat cadence with concurrent async refresh and durable write-failure side channel
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`DEFAULT_INDEPENDENT_HEARTBEAT_MS`, `startIndependentHeartbeat`, durable heartbeat-failure marker reader); core/scripts/loop/supervisor.ts (`driveSupervisor` wiring, `independentHeartbeatMs`, `independentHeartbeatSleep`); process fields in core/scripts/loop/types.ts (`LoopSupervisorProcess.heartbeat_at`); separate durable failure marker (not only in-memory `heartbeat_write_error`)

alternatives.option: Keep only cycle-end heartbeat refresh
alternatives.rejected_because: Long blocking whole-item dispatch stalls cycle-bound refresh and makes a live process look dead; acceptance requires independent cadence during dispatch/wait/backoff.

alternatives.option: Infer liveness solely from model/worker progress messages
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance forbids requiring model/worker progress messages for heartbeat advance.

alternatives.option: Share `recoverySleep` for independent heartbeat sleeps
alternatives.rejected_because: Would couple recovery-backoff accounting/tests to liveness cadence; supervisor explicitly separates the channels.

alternatives.option: Record heartbeat_write_error only on the same process-identity write that just failed (prior d4 wording)
alternatives.rejected_because: A failed process-record write cannot durably publish its own failure field; a separate status process would still read a prior fresh heartbeat_at and report healthy liveness (challenge 39e18c4b).

alternatives.option: Require a dedicated OS thread/process for heartbeat independent of the Node event loop
alternatives.rejected_because: Production dispatch is Promise-based harness wait (subprocess/I/O) and yields the event loop; concurrent async heartbeat is sufficient. A second OS process is out of scope complexity.

assumptions: Controller holds the run lock and owns process-identity persistence while driving.
Default wall-clock interval of 15s is an acceptable production bound; tests inject shorter intervals and sleeps.
`dispatchItem` and other long controller waits are async (Promise) and yield the Node event loop during child/I/O wait so the concurrent heartbeat task can run.
A durable failure marker path can succeed when the process-identity write path fails, or its failure is itself observable as non-healthy (never silently healthy).
invariants: Heartbeat refreshes on bounded independent cadence without model progress messages.
Independent heartbeat is a concurrent async task started before the cycle/dispatch loop (`startIndependentHeartbeat` + injectable sleep), not a cooperative callback inside `dispatchItem`.
Refresh stops after lock loss / terminal exit (`shouldContinue` / `stop()`).

Failed heartbeat persistence MUST be visible to a separate status invocation: write a durable side-channel failure marker (distinct file/path/seam from the process-identity record) on write failure; status reads that marker and classifies process_liveness as `write_failed` / coarse non-healthy even when the last successful `heartbeat_at` is still inside the liveness bound.
In-memory-only `heartbeat_write_error` is insufficient alone for cross-process visibility; it may remain as a local cache but is not the authority for status.

If both process-identity write and failure-marker write fail, status MUST NOT report healthy liveness solely from a stale-but-within-bound prior heartbeat while the controller still claims to be driving; prefer `write_failed`/`unknown` with durable attribution when the marker is present, else insufficient-evidence `unknown` rather than healthy when independent refresh is overdue relative to configured cadence + bound policy documented in tests.
evidence: core/scripts/loop/supervisor.ts: `startIndependentHeartbeat` concurrent with `runSupervisorCycle` / `await dispatchItem` (Promise dispatch seam).
core/scripts/factory-status.ts: independent heartbeat loop uses injectable sleep; recovery backoff uses separate `recoverySleep` channel.
Prior gap: write-failure path only `setRecord({heartbeat_write_error})` without durable side channel (factory-status.ts catch; supervisor cycle catch) — revised by this decision.
openspec/.../specs/controller-independent-health/spec.md: independent cadence and failed-persistence requirements.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 4.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Currently wired on the durable loop supervisor path; #890 macro-controller must adopt the same heartbeat + failure-marker seams when it owns the run. Not a cross-host liveness claim. Not a multi-threaded runtime redesign.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on the 15s default vs write contention under heavy store I/O; falsified if independent writes cause measurable lock/store thrash or if 15s is too coarse for external supervisors. Low on concurrent-async sufficiency for Promise-based dispatch; falsified only if production introduces multi-second synchronous CPU holds on the controller event loop without yielding.

decisions.title: Three independent health dimensions; dead requires identity-bound same-host absence (pid+boot, service-aware)
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`classifyFactoryHealth`, `FactoryStatusHealthDimensions`, `DEFAULT_LIVENESS_BOUND_MS`, process_liveness/durable_progress/expected_waiting/coarse, probes: `isPidAlive`, `isServiceActive?`, identity fields hostname/pid/boot_id/service_controller); public JSON `health` block

alternatives.option: Single boolean "alive" / "stuck" conflating wait and wedge
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires process liveness, durable progress, and expected waiting as separable dimensions.

alternatives.option: Classify stuck from wall-clock age of last event alone
alternatives.rejected_because: Creates false positives on long legal waits (CI, provider cooldown, backoff, capacity, human).

alternatives.option: Classify dead from stale heartbeat alone, including cross-host holders
alternatives.rejected_because: Single-host process evidence cannot prove remote death; design and concurrency scope forbid cross-host death claims.

alternatives.option: Classify dead from stale heartbeat + pid-absent only (prior d5 wording)
alternatives.rejected_because: Underspecified for service-managed controllers and PID reuse: a restarted service with a new controller process can leave a stale prior pid absent while the service is live; an unrelated process can also occupy a reused pid. Challenge de7f2937.

assumptions: Process identity authoritative binding is (hostname, pid, boot_id) on the process-identity record; optional service identity is `service_controller` (or equivalent unit name) when macro/service-managed.
Same-host hostname match is required before any local process/service probe is trusted for death.
Operations used for stuck detection are explicitly started with both start time and deadline recorded.
Liveness bound default 90s is the freshness window for independent heartbeats.
invariants: `suspected_stuck` requires live liveness AND explicitly started operation past deadline AND no durable progress since operation start AND not healthy waiting before a wait deadline.

`dead` requires ALL of: (1) heartbeat stale/absent past bound, (2) same-host hostname match, (3) recorded controller process absence proof that is identity-bound — pid not alive OR (when boot_id/service binding is required by available evidence) proof the live pid is not the recorded controller boot/service instance, (4) when a service_controller identity is present in sources, service absence proof OR joint proof that the service is not running the recorded controller identity; a running service with a replaced controller process alone MUST NOT classify as `dead` (classify `unknown` until the new identity is observed or the service is stopped).

PID reuse: pid-alive without binding evidence that the live process is the recorded boot_id/controller instance is insufficient for `dead` and insufficient for healthy live upgrade from stale — prefer `unknown`.
Cross-host or insufficient evidence is `unknown`, never `dead`.
Expected wait with future deadline is healthy waiting, not stuck.
Heartbeat write failure (via durable failure marker per d4) surfaces as non-healthy (`write_failed` / coarse `unknown`), not healthy liveness.

Classification matrix tests (injected probes) cover: stale+pid absent+no service → dead; stale+pid absent+service active → unknown; stale+pid alive (reuse) → unknown; stale+service stopped → dead when service identity present; cross-host → unknown; probes unavailable → unknown.
evidence: Prior classifyFactoryHealth upgraded stale→dead on same_host && pidAlive===false only (factory-status.ts) — insufficient for service restart / PID reuse (challenge de7f2937).
LoopSupervisorProcess already carries boot_id for restart distinction (loop/types.ts) but was unused in dead classification — revised to use it.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 5 and controller-independent-health dead/unknown scenarios; concurrency scope single-host only.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not authorize automated remediation (kill/restart) from `suspected_stuck`/`dead`; classification is observational only. Not a multi-host consensus health model. Service probe is host-local (e.g. systemd unit state) when service identity is present; no remote orchestrator claims.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on exact service-manager probe shape until #890 service records stabilize; falsified if production service identity cannot map into injected `isServiceActive` without live non-injectable I/O in unit tests. Low on the stuck/waiting rules (acceptance-locked).

decisions.title: Owned expected-wait lifecycle for every acceptance wait kind; optional process fields legacy-safe
decisions.surface: core/scripts/loop/types.ts (`LoopExpectedWaitKind`, optional process fields); core/scripts/loop/supervisor.ts (`markControllerOperation` as sole process-identity wait writer; concrete call sites); factory-status readers of those fields

alternatives.option: Require a new mandatory process-identity schema version that rejects pre-#891 supervisor.json
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires legacy runs and missing optional sources remain readable with explicit unknown/legacy attribution.

alternatives.option: Store operation/wait evidence only in-memory or only in action-evidence free text
alternatives.rejected_because: Stuck classification needs durable start/deadline/progress timestamps independent of free text; free text is also forbidden on the remote-safe surface.

alternatives.option: Omit default dispatch deadline and only mark operations that callers specially configure
alternatives.rejected_because: Stuck classification cannot fire without an explicit deadline; long dispatches would remain unclassifiable forever.

alternatives.option: Only mark dispatch waits and state that other ops must set their own deadlines without named owners (prior d6 wording)
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance lists CI, provider cooldown, recovery backoff, dependency, capacity, and human waits as healthy-waiting categories; without concrete writers those paths cannot be classified as waiting (challenge eb4a9f68).

assumptions: Process-identity record remains the controller-owned liveness/progress/wait evidence surface (distinct from lock token ownership).
Two-hour default dispatch operation deadline is a coarse backstop, not a product SLA for advance duration.
`markControllerOperation` is the single writer seam for process-identity operation/wait fields.
invariants: Optional fields load on older records without migration.
Owned writers and lifecycle (set → hold with future deadline → clear) without raw reason text:
- `dispatch`: set at whole-item `dispatchItem` start (operation `dispatch_item` + wait kind `dispatch` + default 2h deadline); clear on dispatch success/failure.
- `recovery_backoff`: set in `driveSupervisor` before recovery sleep chunks with deadline = now+min(retryAfter,60s); clear after sleep stretch.
- `capacity`: set when cycle records pure worktree `capacity_wait` / admission stop (`worktree_capacity`) with a future recheck deadline; clear when capacity wait clears or run stops.
- `human`: set when hold-outstanding / blocked_needs_human parks the run with a future check deadline (or explicit hold deadline when present); clear on resume/unblock/terminal.

- `dependency`: set when the controller intentionally idles because the frontier is dependency-gated (not deadlock-stopped) with a future recheck deadline; clear when eligibility unblocks or stop/deadlock terminal is recorded.

- `ci`: set when the controller observes an in-flight item waiting on CI (progress-mirror/stage gate) and upgrades or records wait kind `ci` with a future deadline while still live; clear on CI terminal or dispatch end.

- `provider_cooldown`: set when provider/rate-limit cooldown is observed as the reason the controller waits (provider source or dispatch/policy signal) with cooldown_until as deadline; clear when cooldown ends.

Nested waits during an active dispatch MAY overwrite `expected_wait_kind`/`expected_wait_deadline` with the more specific kind while keeping the dispatch operation id/start/deadline for stuck detection.
Absence of operation deadline cannot yield `suspected_stuck` from age alone.
Wait kinds on the public envelope are allowlisted only (`sanitizeWaitKind`); no free-text reasons.
evidence: Already implemented: dispatch start/clear and recovery_backoff set/clear via markControllerOperation (supervisor.ts).
Types already enumerate all wait kinds (loop/types.ts `LoopExpectedWaitKind`).
Gap closed by this revision: capacity/human/dependency/ci/provider_cooldown lacked process-identity writers despite acceptance and classification tests that only inject those kinds.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 5 false-stuck mitigation; controller-independent-health healthy-waiting scenarios.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not change lock ownership or advance-stage internal deadlines. Does not require campaign-specific (#654) progress ownership. Deadlock terminal stops are stop records, not expected waits.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on exact default recheck deadlines for capacity/human/dependency/ci when upstream signals lack an explicit deadline — implementation MUST pick a bounded documented default per kind rather than omit the deadline (omission prevents healthy-waiting classification). Falsified if production signals routinely lack usable deadline bases and defaults systematically misclassify.

decisions.title: Honest cost/telemetry tri-state; no quota or zero-cost invention
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`CostCoverageKind`, envelope `cost` block, provider source forbidding `remaining_quota_percent`)

alternatives.option: Emit 0 cost or 100% remaining quota when telemetry is missing for prettier dashboards
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance forbids remaining-quota percentage and zero-cost inference from absence; missing data must stay unknown.

alternatives.option: Omit the cost block entirely when data is missing
alternatives.rejected_because: Snapshot field checklist expects cost coverage present as actual/estimated/unknown with attribution rather than silent absence.

assumptions: Upstream cost sources, when present, already distinguish actual vs estimated vs unknown.
Provider cooldown is a separate boolean/deadline signal, not a quota percentage.
invariants: Cost coverage is only `actual` | `estimated` | `unknown`.
Assembler does not invent remaining-quota percentages or zero USD from missing sources.
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts: `CostCoverageKind`, `FactoryCostSource` / `FactoryProviderSource` comments forbidding remaining_quota_percent.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 6.
Issue acceptance criteria and proposal honesty section.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not implement a cost accounting system; only projects allowlisted coverage fields when provided.
decisions.uncertainty: Low. Falsified if a later product requirement mandates inventing synthetic cost/quota and contradicts this issue.

decisions.title: Graceful #890 absence: loop supervisor primary when macro-controller missing
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`FactoryMacroControllerSource` optional, controller.kind macro|loop_supervisor|unknown, run/controller attribution); CLI assembly path in pipeline.ts

alternatives.option: Block #891 until #890 macro-controller is always present in production
alternatives.rejected_because: Issue depends on #890 for full identity but acceptance requires readable status with explicit unknown/legacy for missing optional controller fields.

alternatives.option: Invent synthetic macro-controller identity when none is running
alternatives.rejected_because: Design Decision 7 forbids inventing a macro-controller that is not running.

assumptions: Narrow #890-shaped interface is sufficient to fill identity/mode/revision/contract when present.
Loop supervisor process identity + durable loop status remain available for pre-#890 and hybrid deployments.
invariants: Missing macro controller yields explicit attribution, not fabricated service identity.
Status remains pure observation over whatever subset of sources exists.
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts: optional `macroController` source and controller/run attribution paths.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 7 and Impact section.
proposal.md depends-on #890 with legacy-safe readability.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not implement #890 service control; only consumes a narrow read projection when available. Campaign-specific progress (#654) is out of scope.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium until #890 production shapes stabilize; falsified if real #890 records cannot map into `FactoryMacroControllerSource` without expanding mutation or secret-bearing fields into the public envelope.
